messages.subject: pcountOpen: trend vs constant dynamics
parts:
Hi all,

 First off, thanks to those who post answers on this forum, and an especially big thanks to those who developed Unmarked and consistently answer questions from beginners such as myself.

 I am struggling to fit a somewhat complex dataset using pcountOpen (107 sites; 14 primary periods [years, unevenly spaced]; 15-20 secondary periods [depending on closure assumptions for each of several species]; apparently low detectability; many site, yearly, and observation covariates).  I am interested in the effects of timber harvests on population growth or decline for multiple species over time.  The models seemed to be converging with the default dynamics settings, but once I started using dynamics = “trend” I started getting a lot more ‘Hessian is singular,’ ‘Hessian is not invertible,’ etc. messages, as well as runtimes on the order of hours for null models and >20hrs for models with covariates.  Following this, I started wondering if I could just use constant dynamics and derive population trends from changes in survival and recruitment over time.

 I ran the simulated example from the manual, and found that the trend and constant dynamics resulted in different estimates of initial abundance and detection probability.  Moreover, I found that while the dynamics=constant models seemed insensitive to K, the trend models seemed sensitive to K, both in model fit and parameter estimates (this echoes my preliminary work with my data, though for my data the trend models that did run had lower AIC values than constant models).  Below is my code for the simulated data:

 

> set.seed(3)

> M <- 50   

> T <- 5    

> lambda <- 4

> gamma <- 1.5

> omega <- 0.8

> p <- 0.7 

> y <- N <- matrix(NA, M, T) 

> S <- G <- matrix(NA, M, T-1)

> N[,1] <- rpois(M, lambda)  

> for(t in 1:(T-1)) {

+   S[,t] <- rbinom(M, N[,t], omega)

+   G[,t] <- rpois(M, gamma)

+   N[,t+1] <- S[,t] + G[,t]

+ }

> y[] <- rbinom(M*T, N, p)

> umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(y= y, numPrimary=T)

> summary(umf)

My questions:

1)      1)  Should the parameter estimates for initial abundance and detection match for constant vs trend dynamics based on the same simulated dataset?

2)      2)   If data is not converging well for trend dynamics, could one derive trend estimates using survival/recruitment from constant models?  How much does this represent poor practice if trend dynamics make biological sense and null models with trend dynamics have better AIC scores?  (For my data, I’ve tried increasing K, and adding start values from models that did seem to converge, but the run times get longer and don’t seem to improve model convergence.  Likewise I tried to run models using obsCovs to better model detection, which did improve AIC scores, but still resulted in dismal estimates of detection (<0.02), non-convergence, and frighteningly long run times).

       Many thanks, 

        Alex

Hi all,

Perhaps my long original post is discouraging responses, so I'll re-post with a (hopefully) simple question:

In pcountOpen, should the parameter estimates for initial abundance and detection match for constant vs trend dynamics based on the same simulated dataset?

If anyone has any ideas on this question I'd be grateful for a response.

Thanks!
-Alex

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: pcountOpen: trend vs constant dynamics
parts:
hi Alex,
 
 I don't think they should match, in general, when you modify some other component of the model.
 
 I also think K = 20 is generally too low and it is not surprising to see sensitivity to K when it is set so low. Keep K = 100 or more and then evaluate sensitivity by trying some models with K = 150.
 
 This class of models is extremely complicated and numerical errors are to be expected with small to moderate data sets and any complexity at all.  Good starting values can be extremely important. There are not general procedures or rules of thumb for practical use of this class of models because it is relatively new and not too many people are working on it. 
 
regards
andy
